<reason>B built the cleaner path to victory by forcing a live comparison—continuity of memory versus continuity of honor—and holding A to a contradiction A never fully escaped: names as still-civic models when inflating the motion, fossils when denying harm. A landed real pressure on administrability and “primarily,” and the fossil/scar frame was distinctive, but B’s answers plus the junta consistency argument made the proposition easier to affirm than A made it to reject. A’s clipped opening was a modest execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s R1 dilemma (heritage when useful, “just an address” when indefensible), pressed again in Q1 and R2: if every eponym is still a civic model, governments are still awarding honor; if honor has drained, continuity of honor is not at stake.</best_rebuttal>
